text:
sarah: Heads-up — invoice-preview is showing ~1.8% positive delta for today vs yesterday for a slice of EU tenants. Not obvious in the dashboard yet.
mike: ack, saw a spike in late-arrival events in the metering consumer at ~02:05 UTC. Likely related to the new connector patch rolled 02:00.
anita: Which connector? the 'priority-queue-connector' change that switched to scoped acking?
jon: yea that PR toggled `ack_on_enqueue` -> `ack_on_commit` and added a small retry buffer. I wondered about watermark handling.
sarah: exact. The issue shows invoices inflated because preview window counts include late-arrival events that should have been attributed to previous hour.
mike: reproduction: run local ingest with slower downstream and you'll see reorder. Patch diff had this block:
```
// changed behavior
if (ack_on_commit) {
  enqueue(event)
} else {
  ack(event)
}
```
Looks fine but we don't set `event.embedding_scope` until commit in a few code paths.
anita: So dedupe key or fingerprint might be computed after enqueue, causing double-counts when the retry path sends earlier partials?
jon: Correct. If a prior attempt was enqueued with no fingerprint and later commit sets fingerprint, aggregation can treat them as separate tokens.
sarah: Can we short-term stop counting late-arrivals in invoice-preview? I don't want biz to see noisy billing previews.
mike: We could add a conservative preview filter: ignore events with `ingest_latency_ms > 30_000` for preview calculations. Simple flag in preview aggregator.
anita: That'll hide some real usage during infra incidents though. But acceptable as rollback mitigation.
ops-runbook-bot: Note: Preview filters should not affect final invoices. Add note to runbook: "Preview filter applied — disconnect if discrepancy > 0.5%".
jon: Long term we should compute fingerprint deterministically at enqueue or materialize a stable dedupe_id earlier. Moving `fingerprint` computation into the proxy that serializes the event avoids this class of dupes.
sarah: Agreed. Plan proposal:
1) Short-term: patch preview aggregator to ignore events where `ingest_latency_ms > 30s` (canary on 5% tenants)
2) Medium: revert to ack-on-enqueue while we refactor fingerprinting OR change pipeline so fingerprint is included before enqueue
3) Console: add a 'preview-confidence' metric and explanation tooltip so PMs see when preview suppressed
4) Rollout: 5% canary -> 25% -> 100% with telemetry checks: preview_delta and late_event_rate

mike: I'll open the hotfix PR for preview filter now. Will include a job metric `preview_filter_applied_count`.
anita: I'll work on the fingerprint PR and test harness for reordering scenarios.
jon: I'll add a small dashboard card in Console under Billing -> Preview: showing `preview_confidence` (green/orange/red) and examples of suppressed events.
sarah: For alerts, let's create alert `billing.preview_delta > 1% for 15m` and route to #eng-oncall and #finance-watch. Also set a runbook link.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: hotfix/preview-filter -> staging
mike: pushing now.
deploy-bot: deploy started: hotfix/preview-filter to staging (build 5482)
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: hotfix/preview-filter to staging (build 5482)
mike: staged a canary for 5% tenants, starting monitoring. tagging onboarded tenants for backfill check.
anita: FYI, the fingerprint refactor will include this API change to event envelope: `dedupe_id` becomes required. I'll draft migration notes for Dedicated customers.
sarah: Thanks — keep finance looped. I'll post a short explainer to #product and ping finance ops.
jon: PRs:
- hotfix: github.com/redwood/hotfixes/preview-filter#548
- fingerprint: github.com/redwood/ingest/fingerprint-refactor#22

sarah: tl;dr: short fix applied, longer refactor in progress, console UX to improve transparency, rollout plan with metrics and alerts. Anything else?
mike: we'd also want a nightly job to reconcile late-arrival attribution and emit a correction metric for invoices. I'll add that to backlog.
anita: ok, assigning tasks and will pair with jon tomorrow for the dashboard copy.
sarah: thanks all. closing thread once staging looks stable.
